issues.description: The problem description contains conflicting specifications for the Milkable.messageOnMilk method. In the UML and earlier interface description the method is shown without parameters (messageOnMilk(): String), but later in Part 2 the text explicitly requires messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and specifies a return string containing the milk volume. The provided solution and template code follow the no-argument signature (messageOnMilk()) and implementations that do not accept or print a volume. This discrepancy will confuse students about which signature to implement and can lead to compilation errors if they implement the version required by the textual description while the codebase/tests expect the no-argument version.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the mismatch by choosing one signature and making all artifacts consistent. Either: (A) Update the problem statement Part 2 text to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and remove the volume formatting from the example return string; or (B) update the Milkable interface and all implementing classes (Seal, Goat, and any usages) to messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and adjust tests/Main and solution code to pass and display the volume (e.g., return "<Type> <name> is milked (volume: " + milkVolume + "L)"). Ensure the UML, textual description, interfaces, and implementations are aligned.
